identification.name: Aluminum 7075-T6
identification.common_form_notes: Widely stocked as plate, sheet, and bar. Typically purchased in T6 or T651 temper (stress-relieved plate). Not recommended for welding in most applications.
identification.notes: Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy (7xxx series). T6 temper: solution heat-treated and artificially aged. The highest-strength commonly available aluminum alloy. Susceptible to stress-corrosion cracking (SCC) in sustained tensile loading — T73 or T7351 tempers provide better SCC resistance at the cost of ~15% strength reduction. Not recommended for fusion welding. All mechanical properties from MIL-HDBK-5J (U.S. Military Handbook 5J, freely available); eFunda linked for cross-reference. Cryogenic CTE (coefficient of thermal expansion) table entries (−196 to −100 °C) are instantaneous values from the NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) Cryogenic Materials Database polynomial for wrought aluminium alloys (6061-T6 polynomial used as proxy; dedicated 7075 polynomial not published — all wrought Al alloys agree within ±4%). Above-RT CTE from MIL-HDBK-5J. Melting point is solidus (477°C); liquidus 635°C (MIL-HDBK-5J). Fatigue S-N curve (4 points, R=−1 fully reversed) is computed from MIL-HDBK-5J's best-fit equivalent-stress equation for unnotched 7075-T6 bare sheet, 0.090 in., electropolished, axial loading (Figure 3.7.6.1.8(d); sample size 176, R²=80%): Log Nf = 14.86 − 5.80·log(Seq), Seq = Smax·(1−R)^0.49. Solved at R=−1 for Smax at 1e5/1e6/1e7/5e8 cycles — same product form, methodology, and life points as aluminum-2024-t3's curve, for direct comparability. Replaces a previously stored curve (310/230/165/152 MPa) that did not reproduce this same-cited-source equation at any consistent R when back-solved (implied R ranged from −0.61 to −1.10 against the rod/bar equation and −0.25 to +0.73 against this sheet equation) — its actual origin is unknown, so it was discarded rather than kept alongside a properly verified curve. The 5×10⁸-cycle point extrapolates beyond the equation's directly-tested life range; treat it as approximate per MIL-HDBK-5J's own caution note on equivalent-stress extrapolation.

typical_usage: Aerospace structural members, aircraft fittings and bulkheads, high-performance bicycle frames, rock climbing equipment, competitive cycling components, and any application requiring maximum specific strength in aluminum.
